import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 337

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/337](https://www.erdosproblems.com/337)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [ErGr80b] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L., *On bases with an exact order*. Acta Arith. (1980),
  201-207.
- [RT85] Ruzsa, I. Z. and Turjányi, S., *A note on additive bases of integers*. Publ. Math.
  Debrecen (1985), 101-104.
- [Tu84] Turjányi, S., *A note on basis sequences*. Topics in classical number theory, Vol. I, II
  (Budapest, 1981) (1984), 1571-1576.
-/

namespace Erdos337

open Filter Set Asymptotics

open scoped Pointwise

/--
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be an additive basis (of any finite order) such that
$\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert=o(N)$. Is it true that
$$
\lim_{N\to \infty}\frac{\lvert (A+A)\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}
{\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}=\infty?
$$

The answer is no, and a counterexample was provided by Turjányi [Tu84]. This was generalised (to
the replacement of $A+A$ by the $h$-fold sumset $hA$ for any $h\geq 2$) by Ruzsa and Turjányi
[RT85].

"Additive basis" is `Set.IsAsymptoticAddBasis`: some finite $h$ has $hA$ containing every
sufficiently large integer. The exact notion `Set.IsAddBasis`, which asks that $hA$ be all of
$\mathbb{N}$, would force $0, 1 \in A$ and is not the class these results are about.

The linked file states the basis hypothesis as `∃ N₀, Set.Ici N₀ ⊆ iterated_sumset A k` and
indexes both counting functions by a real $x$ through $\lfloor x\rfloor$, where the counting
functions here are indexed by $N : \mathbb{N}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/68da20b96673899166e94638f5a7fffeb7231d35/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos337.lean"]
theorem erdos_337 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.IsAsymptoticAddBasis →
      (fun N : ℕ ↦ ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ)) →
      Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦ (((A + A) ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ) / ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ))
        atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
This was generalised (to the replacement of $A+A$ by the $h$-fold sumset $hA$ for any $h\geq 2$)
by Ruzsa and Turjányi [RT85].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_337.variants.h_fold : ∀ h : ℕ, 2 ≤ h →
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.IsAsymptoticAddBasis ∧
      (fun N : ℕ ↦ ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ)) ∧
      ¬ Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦
          ((h • A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ) / ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ))
        atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Ruzsa and Turjányi do prove (under the same hypotheses) that
$$
\lim_{N\to \infty}\frac{\lvert (A+A+A)\cap \{1,\ldots,3N\}\rvert}
{\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}=\infty,
$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_337.variants.three_fold :
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.IsAsymptoticAddBasis →
      (fun N : ℕ ↦ ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ)) →
      Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦
          (((A + A + A) ∩ Icc 1 (3 * N)).ncard : ℝ) / ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ))
        atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Ruzsa and Turjányi do prove (under the same hypotheses) that
$$
\lim_{N\to \infty}\frac{\lvert (A+A+A)\cap \{1,\ldots,3N\}\rvert}
{\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}=\infty,
$$
and conjecture that the same should be true with $(A+A)\cap \{1,\ldots,2N\}$ in the numerator.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_337.variants.ruzsa_turjanyi :
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.IsAsymptoticAddBasis →
      (fun N : ℕ ↦ ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun N : ℕ ↦ (N : ℝ)) →
      Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦
          (((A + A) ∩ Icc 1 (2 * N)).ncard : ℝ) / ((A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard : ℝ))
        atTop atTop := by
  sorry

end Erdos337

status_issues.source_status: This is a positive consequence of the classical Plünnecke inequality, not an open problem. RT85 explicitly reduces its Conjecture 1 to its finite-set Conjecture 2. Ruzsa's later survey records precisely that finite-set bound, with f(s,k)=s^k. I did not establish when this particular corollary was first explicitly noted.
status_issues.evidence: RT85, §3, p. 102: 'In a similar way we could deduce Conjecture 1 from Conjecture 2,' where Conjecture 2 asks for |kX|≤f(s,k)|X| when |2X|=s|X|. Ruzsa, Sumsets and structure, Chapter 1, Corollary 2.4 and Exercise 13, explicitly gives |kX|≤s^k|X|. URLs: https://publi.math.unideb.hu/paper/3707/download/ and https://www.math.cmu.edu/users/af1p/Teaching/AdditiveCombinatorics/Additive-Combinatorics.pdf . Directly for the Lean statement, take X=A∩[0,N] and let h be a basis order. Then N−O(1)≤|hX|≤(|2X|/|X|)^h|X|. Since |X|=A(N)+O(1)=o(N) and |2X|≤|(A+A)∩[1,2N]|+1, the displayed ratio must tend to infinity.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the category to research solved. Keep the mathematical statement unchanged, and explain that the conjecture posed in RT85 follows from Plünnecke's inequality, with an appropriate reference.

reformulations.difference: The linked formal proof uses a recursively defined iterated sumset, an explicit tail-covering basis condition, and counting functions indexed by real x through the natural floor. The reviewed statement uses Set.IsAsymptoticAddBasis and natural-number indexing.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The recursive sumset equals h • A. On ℕ, cofinite equals atTop, so the basis condition is exactly ∃ h N₀, Ici N₀ ⊆ h • A. A sequence f tends to +∞ iff x ↦ f(⌊x⌋₊) does: compose with floor in one direction and the natural-to-real embedding in the other. Likewise f(N)=o(N) iff f(⌊x⌋₊)=o(x), using floor(x)≤x eventually. The full equivalence between the external proposition and the reviewed right-hand side was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean. Thus the external theorem's negation supports the recorded answer(False).

reformulations.difference: The primary papers define an asymptotic basis using at most a fixed number of summands, whereas Set.IsAsymptoticAddBasis requires exactly a fixed number. These are different classes of sets but give equivalent versions of this question.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a weak asymptotic basis A, put B=A∪{0}. Padding with zeros makes B an exact-order asymptotic basis. Its positive counting function is unchanged, and (B+B)∩[1,N]=((A+A)∩[1,N])∪(A∩[1,N]). Consequently the two ratios differ by a quantity between 0 and 1 once the denominator is positive. They therefore tend to +∞ simultaneously. Every exact-order basis is also a weak basis, establishing equivalence of the universal questions and their negations.

reformulations.difference: The formalization again uses exact-order rather than at-most-order asymptotic bases. This does not change the existence of a counterexample for any fixed h≥2.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Adjoin zero to a weak basis A, obtaining an exact basis B with the same positive counting function. Choose a positive a∈A. Write C_j(X)=|jA∩[1,X]|. For 1≤j≤h, padding with h−j copies of a gives C_j(X)≤C_h(X)+(h−j)a. Since hB is the union of jA for 0≤j≤h, its positive count lies between C_h(X) and h C_h(X)+a h(h−1)/2. Dividing by A(N), which tends to infinity, shows that the h-fold ratio for A diverges iff the ratio for B diverges. Thus zero-adjoining preserves counterexamples; the reverse implication follows from inclusion of the basis classes.

reformulations.difference: RT85's Theorem 2 permits at-most-order asymptotic bases; Lean uses exact-order asymptotic bases.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For B=A∪{0}, the basis and density conditions transfer as above. Fix a positive a∈A and put C_3(X)=|3A∩[1,X]|. Padding shorter sums gives C_3(X)≤|3B∩[1,X]|≤3C_3(X)+3a. Taking X=3N and dividing by the unchanged A(N) proves equivalence of divergence for A and B. Hence restricting the universal assertion to exact-order bases loses no mathematical content.

reformulations.difference: RT85's Conjecture 1 allows at-most-order asymptotic bases, rather than the exact-order bases used in Lean.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For B=A∪{0} and a positive a∈A, padding one-term sums gives |A∩[1,X]|≤|(A+A)∩[1,X]|+a. Therefore |(A+A)∩[1,X]|≤|(B+B)∩[1,X]|≤2|(A+A)∩[1,X]|+a. At X=2N the denominators for A and B are identical and tend to infinity, so divergence is equivalent. Zero-adjoining and inclusion of the basis classes establish equivalence of the universal formulations.

review.notes: All four mathematical declarations were checked; no misformalization was found. Lean experiments compiled successfully in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, including the full external-statement equivalence, h-fold notation and intersection scope, finite counting sets, exclusion of finite/zero-order bases, eventual positivity of the denominator, a small ratio equal to 1/2, and the equivalence of answer(False) with the h=2 counterexample formulation. The hypotheses are nonvacuous (squares give a zero-density basis). The live Erdős site was Cloudflare-blocked, so its statement and remarks were read through the August 24 archive; the current community database confirms the main problem's negative, Lean-formalized status. The archived page still describes the Ruzsa–Turjányi variant historically as a conjecture; the status correction above is substantiated by RT85's explicit reduction and Ruzsa's later survey. The standalone Tu84 paper could not be obtained, but its counterexample and the generalization are explicitly confirmed in RT85. No checkout files were edited.
